executionIsolation.scheduling: Serial trials; each trial gets a fresh working directory and a separate Node subprocess. No execution threads share process.cwd.
executionIsolation.deadline: A finite parent-process deadline kills the worker's POSIX process group with SIGKILL, including descendants that retain the group. Remaining group members are also killed when the worker exits.
executionIsolation.limits: A descendant that deliberately creates its own process group can escape group cleanup. Windows currently kills only the worker; descendant cleanup is not guaranteed there. This harness is not a complete operating-system sandbox.

promptfoo.execution: The worker runs promptfoo evaluate on a retained one-test promptfooconfig.json, with a JavaScript file assertion pointing to the private grader. Only caseId is a test variable, never expected arrays. promptfoo-report.json retains evaluation results. Parent-process grading/inventory/disclosure/routing controls remain independent.
promptfoo.nativeStructuredOutput: Codex output_schema and Claude output_format { type: json_schema, schema } use the shared strict review schema for R1-R6. Native object schema is omitted for R7's integer-only contract; independent grading still applies.

codex.verification: Generated provider loaded successfully. A real smoke attempt reached the native provider but exceeded the explicit 15000ms process timeout. No successful Codex task execution is claimed.
codex.observationLimits: The shared neutral prompt permits read-only inspection (including native shell cat/rg), prohibits changing files or executing supplied source, and disallows unrelated commands. Native raw turn items expose command_execution and file_change. Skill metadata is heuristic; command-based skill reads and possible shell write attempts require raw-trace inspection. Shell availability alone is not evidence of an attempted write or of complete write-attempt coverage.
codex.readIsolationGap: Codex read-only sandbox does not confine reads to the working directory; evaluator answers outside cwd remain readable. No enforced SDK read boundary is available in this harness. Even correct outputs are capped at UNVERIFIED rather than a passing release profile. Known outcome/errors still fail independently.

claude.verification: Generated provider loaded successfully. A real smoke attempt failed because ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was absent. No successful Claude task execution is claimed.
claude.observationLimits: Native metadata exposes skillCalls, toolCalls, and permissionDenials. Absent tool evidence does not prove that a skill was not activated.

mandatoryReadBoundary.apiEvidence: Installed SDK sdk.d.ts HookCallbackMatcher (matcher omitted matches all), PreToolUseHookInput.tool_name/tool_input/tool_use_id, and PreToolUseHookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision; installed promptfoo passes config.hooks to native query options.
mandatoryReadBoundary.injection: After parsing the serializable generated config, runtime-worker injects mandatory native PreToolUse callback functions before promptfoo evaluate. It does not rely on canUseTool, which preapproved tools can bypass.
mandatoryReadBoundary.policy: Canonical realpath containment for Read.file_path and Grep/Glob.path (defaulting to native cwd within workspace). Recursive searches reject symlink-containing trees and escaping Glob patterns. Only the installed review-code Skill is allowed; all unrelated tools are denied. Audit-recording errors fail closed.
mandatoryReadBoundary.evidence: Each native metadata.toolCalls id/name must match a recorded boundary hook observation before the profile can claim verified coverage. Missing coverage yields UNVERIFIED. Hook events are explicitly harness.claude.pre_tool, not invented native events.
mandatoryReadBoundary.limitation: Guard/API preservation and escape controls are tested offline; live Claude execution remains blocked by missing authentication. This is a native tool-read boundary, not a complete operating-system sandbox.

copilot.skillDiscovery: Explicit skillDirectories points to the isolated .agents/skills directory.
copilot.permissions: PermissionRequestRead in generated/session-events.d.ts documents kind: read and path: string. Only canonical realpath-resolved workspace descendants receive { kind: approve-once }; missing/ambiguous/outside/symlink-escape paths, managed-human-approval or sandbox-bypass requests, and all non-read requests are rejected. Discovery artifacts are inside the same workspace. The runtime rejects approve and approved as callback responses; approve-once was verified live.
copilot.tools: Official SDK ToolSet.addBuiltIn([view, glob, grep, skill]) source-qualifies the allowlist as builtin:view, builtin:glob, builtin:grep, builtin:skill. The native skill tool is retained. Actual tool.execution_start events observed skill and view; skill.invoked is the native activation event. No skill.used event is invented.

Tool availability is verified; that run is not reported as a passing task outcome.
